subject: MSA — insurance coverage matrix, additional insured interpretation & issuance plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Green (Acme Risk) <alex.green@acmerisk.com>, Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@clientcorp.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T15:02:00Z
Subject: MSA — insurance coverage matrix, additional insured interpretation & issuance plan

Team,

We have updated MSA redlines from ClientCorp and there are a few insurance items that need quick alignment before we pass to legal for final sign-off:

1) Coverage minima: ClientCorp wants 5M/10M/2M (GL/Auto/PD) but their order form references our standard 3M/5M/1M. Confirm whether underwriting can bridge the delta or if we need a one-off exception.

2) Additional Insured: their counsel insists on the wording to include “ClientCorp, its affiliates and their respective officers, directors and employees.” Our standard endorsement names only the contracting entity. Is there an endorsement we can issue that matches their ask or do we ask for narrowing language?

3) Claims-made vs occurrence: the redline asks for occurrence for Professional Liability. Our carrier currently issues PL on a claims-made basis with retroactive date — need to confirm if retroactivation/retro date language is acceptable to ClientCorp.

4) Evidence delivery: they want COI and endorsements delivered at countersign / within 3 business days of effective date. We typically deliver COI at signing and endorsement within 10 business days. Can Acme Risk confirm issuance SLAs and what we can commit to?

Attachments: redline_snapshot.pdf (key clauses called out). Alex — can you provide a sample COI and draft endorsement that would satisfy the expanded "additional insured" language, or advise on compromise language?

Goal: resolve insurance interpretation and delivery timeline by end of week so legal can finalize the MSA.

Thanks,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Green (Acme Risk) <alex.green@acmerisk.com>, Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@clientcorp.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA — insurance coverage matrix, additional insured interpretation & issuance plan

Thanks Rishi — quick clarifying points: 

- Can we separate the MSA-level requirements (GL/Auto/PL) from the Order Form obligations (e.g., data processing addenda, product-specific limits)? I want to avoid overcommitting across the portfolio.

- For the additional insured ask, if Acme can produce an endorsement that names the contracting entity plus a parent/affiliate carve-in, that may be acceptable. If not, I suggest offering the client the contracting-entity naming plus a statement that we will use reasonable efforts to extend coverage to affiliated entities via endorsement where carrier allows.

From: Alex Green (Acme Risk) <alex.green@acmerisk.com>

Date: 2026-09-21T14:45:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA — insurance coverage matrix, additional insured interpretation & issuance plan

Hi all,

Thanks for the summary. Quick responses from underwriting and carrier ops below: 

- Limits: Carrier can issue a 5M/10M/2M package but it requires a premium endorsement (we can provide cost estimate). We can also provide a temporary limit letter pending binder issuance if timing is tight.

- Additional Insured: The broad language (ClientCorp, its affiliates, and their officers/directors/employees) is non-standard but we can issue an endorsement that names ClientCorp and its subsidiaries as listed entities. Explicitly naming "all affiliates" is typically declined by carriers. If ClientCorp can provide a list of affiliates at signing, we can include them; otherwise we recommend the contracting-entity naming + a covenant to provide endorsements for named affiliates on a reasonable-efforts basis.

- Professional Liability: Underwriter confirms PL is claims-made. They can provide a retroactive date to align with the start of services and will include a prior acts provision if needed. Occurrence coverage is unavailable.

- Timing / issuance SLAs: COI (Certificate of Insurance) — 1 business day after countersign for standard wording. Endorsements — issuance in 7–10 business days once endorsement text is finalized and carrier signs off.

I've attached sample_Certificate.pdf and endorsement_draft.pdf for your review.

Let me know if you'd like me to turn the endorsement draft into final carrier text (this would be the standard broker workflow; ETA 8 business days).

Best,
Alex Green
Senior Account Executive, Acme Risk
alex.green@acmerisk.com
Attachments: sample_Certificate.pdf; endorsement_draft.pdf

From: Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@clientcorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Green (Acme Risk) <alex.green@acmerisk.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA — insurance coverage matrix, additional insured interpretation & issuance plan

Hi Rishi / Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample docs — helpful. A couple of points from our side: 

1) ClientCorp prefers the additional insured language to follow: 
"ClientCorp, its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees and agents, as additional insureds, but only with respect to liability arising out of the operations of the named insured."

2) If the carrier cannot accept an open-ended "affiliates" list, we can provide a named-subsidiaries list at countersign. That will satisfy our procurement/compliance team.

3) Regarding PL, we accept claims-made if a retroactive date equal to or prior to the service start date is in place and we get 60 days' notice clause for cancellation/non-renewal to ClientCorp.

Please confirm whether Acme can add a 60-day cancellation notice and whether Redwood can commit to providing the named-subsidiaries list within 24 hours of countersign if needed.

Regards,
Sarah Levin
Deputy General Counsel, ClientCorp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@clientcorp.com>, Alex Green (Acme Risk) <alex.green@acmerisk.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:32:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA — insurance coverage matrix, additional insured interpretation & issuance plan

Sarah — thanks, that language is clear. Alex — can you confirm carrier will accept 60-day cancellation notice (or provide alternative) and provide ETA for final endorsement text once we confirm whether ClientCorp will supply a named-subsidiaries list at countersign?

We will prepare the list on our side if ClientCorp chooses that route; Laura/Kimberly we may need a brief legal sign-off on the final endorsement text.

I'll summarize next steps in a short doc and share a single-thread action list.

Rishi

From: Alex Green (Acme Risk) <alex.green@acmerisk.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@clientcorp.com>

Date: 2026-09-22T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA — insurance coverage matrix, additional insured interpretation & issuance plan

Confirming: carrier will accept a 60-day cancellation/nonrenewal notice to named insureds and additional insureds (standard endorsement). If ClientCorp supplies a named-subsidiaries list at countersign, we can incorporate those names into the endorsement — ETA endorsement finalization 5 business days after receiving the list. If ClientCorp wants the broader “all affiliates” language, underwriting will likely decline.

I'll draft a concise action list and share it to this thread by EOD.

Alex
